text: Shelton Medical Centre shows 56 claims against zero beds, a single affiliated doctor, and 100 percent of its patient inflow arranged by one broker, David Smith, who operates from the same registered address. Its payouts are 98.2 percent concentrated in one account, and every patient it has ever billed visited once and vanished from the graph. Individually these are honest patterns; jointly — one-doctor roster, one feeder, one account, no returning or cross-referenced patients, a 1.1-year-old registration — they form the paper-clinic signature this rule was built for. An alternative is a legitimate startup clinic wholly dependent on its founding facilitator, but that would still leave some patient overlap with the wider economy, which is absent. Next step: independent verification that the premises at the shared address can deliver 56 procedures, and a freeze on account ACC_001605 disbursements meanwhile.
